reviewer: Kimi independent actual visual comparison of the exact 65x67 source PNG, enlarged existing source-page 14 and targeted source-note crop, complete unchanged 2048x2048 raw RGBA and native note/right-edge crop, full white/cyan/alpha sheet and evidence, and unchanged naiwa.png; checked cap inside frame, covered hair, brows, absence of facial hair and glasses, one mouth, red standing collar without tie, pose, collar, backing, retained right tab and source versus returned mark footprints.

remaining_reasons: The enlarged original note has TWO compact faint upper mark rows and largely blank lower paper. The returned native note instead has THREE upper rows, an additional isolated gray dot below them, and further dark-gray mark clusters at the lower right. Remove the invented third row, isolated dot and lower-right marks; restore only the source-scale two-row upper footprint and original blank areas without adding substitute glyphs or stains.
entries.positive_observation: The dark olive cap remains inside the complete dark frame and retains a small upper gold eagle, larger lower wreath/cockade, gold braid/piping and glossy black visor. Hair remains covered, dark brows are present, and the face has no glasses, moustache or beard, with one reserved serious closed mouth. The dark olive tunic retains its red standing collar and gold-embroidered red tabs without a tie. The rounded chin meets a short broad fitted collar without a stalk or pinching. The dark olive-gray photographic backplate remains opaque, and the small dark right-edge note tab is visibly retained. Full white/cyan comparisons show no visible interior holes, lost backing or working-matte ring; the added note rows/marks are the separate visible rejection reason above.
entries.visible_limitations: Exact tiny cap and collar embroidery motifs and note glyphs are unreadable at 65x67 and are not rejection grounds. The rejection relies on clearly resolved row counts and added lower gray clusters in the native return versus the enlarged original, not on reading lettering, treating ordinary paper texture as writing, or numeric alpha screening.
